name: humid_overcool_1694_window_pause_zeroes
description: A window opens mid-overcool: the door/window pause takes the thermostat, the term is zeroed and no overcool write follows
notes: Three-exercise protocol (CLAUDE.md Sec 10): (a) effectiveness: an overcool that ignored the pause would step to 74 or write a restore into the open window.

(b) docs-production: docs/08-COMPUTATION-REFERENCE.md 'Humid overcool (Issue #1694)' states this rule; production applies it through humid_overcool.decide_overcool and AutomationEngine._command_adjustments (the one setpoint path).
(c) occupant: an open window gets the normal pause; a regression would send cooling commands into an open window.

Issue #1507 review (real-HA tier): the house reads 77.6F while the scenario's AC cools (at least the setpoint + 1.5F, so the real-HA simulated thermostat really starts its compressor and reports cooling, as a real one does) and 73.0F once a run ends (at or below its stop point, so it really stops); a cooling -> fan -> cooling blip under 5 minutes keeps the house warm. Each reading's humidity is recomputed so its dew point is exactly the one this scenario was written with.

Issue #1507 review: the open-window delay is stated (300 s) instead of relying on the FakeHass default of 0 s. With a real delay the overcool term freezes while it runs and the pause then zeroes it on both tiers. When the delay expires, real HA's handler order closes the gate as window_open in the same instant the pause starts (FakeHass: door_window_pause), so the 14:40 overcool_ended row does not pin the reason.

events.note: Muggy house: 77 F at 64 % RH, dew point 63.9 F (at or above the 60 F trigger).
Hot day: the cool band 68-76 F is armed (cool 76 F).
A window opens and stays open past the 10-minute debounce.

assertions.reason: Rule 3: the window pause turns HVAC off after the debounce.
Only the engage write: no step during the debounce (frozen) and no overcool restore over the pause.

The open window ends the 1 F overcool term by the time the pause holds the thermostat. Its reason is gate:door_window_pause or gate:window_open, depending on which of two handlers runs first when the open-window delay expires (real HA runs the overcool check first), and both close the gate the same way; the other two assertions pin what the occupant gets (HVAC paused, no overcool write over the window).
